title: Chess review
transcript:
Come with me to celebrate Aaron Tveit's birthday
by seeing him in Chess on Broadway.
This musical, first presented in the 80s,
is about an American chess master,
a Russian chess master,
and the woman they're in a love triangle with.
But with the backdrop of the Cold War,
it's debatable if they're the main players or if they're just pawns.
This production features a new book,
a stripped back, almost concert-style format,
and an absolutely fire cast.
Everyone knows Aaron Tveit and Lea Michele are vocal powerhouses,
but I'm especially thrilled that more people
are going to wake up to Nicholas Christopher's greatness.
He is amazing in this show.
I already thought he was amazing in Act 1,
but then we got to End Game in Act 2 and I was floored.
He just attacks the score so ferociously
and embodies the role of Anatoly like he was born to play it.
Actually, what I find most thrilling about this production
is how everyone across the board is locked in.
There's not a semblance of holding back,
which is exactly the assignment for a score that's banger after banger.
We need a cast recording like, yesterday.
Now, the story is kind of messy,
but you're in good hands with Bryce Pinkham narrating the plot.
Though I didn't love some of his book material,
particularly the modern references and cheap jokes that feel out of place,
I thought his performance was great
and I wish he got to sing more.
Something else I wish there was more of is
choreography moments for the incredible, mesmerizing ensemble.
One Night in Bangkok is a highlight
for both choreography and production design —
the lighting design for the show is stunning,
and the whole production is quite visually appealing.
Even if you've seen Chess before,
I doubt you've seen it like this.
I can't personally speak to the changes they've made for this revival,
but I can confidently say they've made a great production.
With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Tyler clearly recommends the show despite acknowledging some flaws with the book material. He praises the cast performances enthusiastically and calls it 'a great production', indicating a positive recommendation with caveats.
keyQuote: I can confidently say they've made a great production.
